## Publish gate report

**Going out:** Product page copy for Chamomile and Lemon Balm tea, on the website, to UK shoppers.

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | On the policy list (certificate on file, renewed 2026) |
| "20 plastic-free tea bags" | "Plastic-free" is on the policy list. The count is a product fact the product team checks. |
| "caffeine-free blend" | Product fact (ingredients). Chamomile and lemon balm contain no caffeine. |
| "gentle, honeyed" | Flavour description, not a claim. |

**Regulated claims:** "for the evening" only says when to drink it. It doesn't say the tea helps sleep, relaxes or calms you, so it isn't a health claim. If someone later adds "helps you unwind" or "promotes sleep", that would be a health claim and would need to come out. No price, urgency, environmental or children's content.

**House style:** The copy is warm, plain and unhurried, with no banned words and no AI tells. Score is about 92/100. I changed nothing.

**Disclosure:** This is the brand's own product page, so there is no ad, partnership, affiliate or gifted content to label.

**Fixed:** Nothing needed fixing.

**Needs a decision:** Nothing. One thing to confirm: "honeyed" should describe the flavour. If the blend has no honey in it, that's fine as written, but the product team should be sure it can't be read as an ingredient.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). The draft passes, but it can't go live until Sam gives an explicit yes to this exact text. I haven't recorded any approval.
